events.text: The old elder who nursed you takes you up the mountain at last, to a stair of broken stone and a gate with no doors. She tells you everything: the founding, the three hundred good years, the one bad night. "It was never the halls that made it a sect," she says. "It was the people who came back to them."

choices.text: Promise her you will raise it again

effects.log: You promise, with your hand on the cold stone of the gate. The old elder does not cry. She only nods, as if she had known the answer for a very long time.

choices.text: Ask her to teach you its first form

effects.log: She teaches you the first form of the fallen sect on the broken stair, slowly, the way it was taught to her eighty years ago. Your feet find it quickly.

events.text: A beggar comes to the gate of the sect you raised and asks for rice. While he eats he says, to nobody, that his grandfather buried something in the old well the night the halls burned, and made him swear never to dig it up.

choices.text: Climb down into the old well

effects.log: At the bottom of the well, under a hundred years of silt, is an iron box. Inside, wrapped in oilcloth, is the lost manual of the sect.

choices.text: Ask the beggar to stay, and dig together

effects.log: The two of you dig for three days. When the iron box comes up, the beggar laughs until he cries. You give him a room in the halls for as long as he wants it.

events.text: A scholar from the capital writes to say that a jade slip in the imperial library bears the seal of the sect you raised. Nobody there can read it. He wonders whether anyone still can.

choices.text: Ride to the capital and read it

effects.log: The ride and the bribes to the librarians cost 20 taels. The jade slip is the lost manual itself, copied by a disciple who fled with it. You copy it back, character by character.

choices.text: Invite the scholar to the halls with it

effects.log: The scholar comes, and stays a month, and between the two of you the lost manual is read again for the first time in a hundred years.

events.text: An old man and a girl of sixteen stand at the gate one spring morning. The old man holds out a wooden token, worn smooth: the token of a disciple of the old sect, his father's. "He always said we would come back when the bell rang again," he says.

choices.text: Ring the bell for them

effects.log: You ring the old bell, once, and the sound goes out over the valley. By summer, other tokens have come out of other drawers, and other families are climbing the stair.

choices.text: Take the girl as a disciple at once

effects.log: The girl bows three times on the stone where her great-grandfather bowed. Word of it travels, and others follow her up the stair.

events.text: At a market three provinces away a stranger sees the crest on your sleeve and drops a basket of pears. "My mother's family were of that sect," the stranger says. "We thought it was gone. Is it true? Is the gate open?"

choices.text: Tell them the gate is open to every one of them

effects.log: The stranger carries the news home, and home carries it further. Within the year, the families of the old disciples are on the road.

choices.text: Help pick up the pears first

effects.log: You pick up every pear before you answer. The stranger never forgets it, and tells the story every time the sect is mentioned. The families come back.

events.text: A sect elder comes through the village to test the children for spiritual roots. One by one the others put their hands on the testing stone, and it glows red, blue, green. When you put yours on it, it stays grey. Somebody laughs.

choices.text: Keep your hand on the stone until they stop laughing

effects.log: You keep your hand on the grey stone for an hour, in the sun, until the laughing stops and the elder has to ask you to let go. The elder looks at you for a long time.

choices.text: Ask the elder what a rootless child can do

effects.log: "Train twice as hard for half as much," the elder says, "and hope the heavens get bored of saying no." It is the most honest thing any adult has ever told you.

events.text: In the third hour of a night of stillness the five energies of your body, which have never answered to anything, turn together for the first time: heart and liver, spleen, lungs and kidneys, one wheel. They gather at the centre of you and wait, as if asking what you want them to become. THE FIVE ENERGIES RETURN TO THE ORIGIN.

choices.text: Let it be fire, the heat that never left you

effects.log: It is fire. It was always going to be fire.

choices.text: Let it be water, patient as the years

effects.log: It is water, deep and slow. It fills every empty place in you.

choices.text: Let it be wood, that grows from nothing

effects.log: It is wood, and it grows. You feel it putting out its first leaves.

events.text: Thirty years of training with nothing to hold it, and tonight, on a cold mountain, all of it moves at once. The five energies of the body circle inward and meet, and where there was nothing at the centre of you, something waits to be named. THE FIVE ENERGIES RETURN TO THE ORIGIN.

choices.text: Let it be metal, that every blow has tempered

effects.log: It is metal, struck true by every year you trained without it.

choices.text: Let it be earth, that held you up all along

effects.log: It is earth. It has been under your feet the whole time.

choices.text: Let it be water, patient as the years

effects.log: It is water, deep and slow. It fills every empty place in you.

events.text: An elder with white eyebrows has watched you across the hall for a whole evening. At last the elder crosses over and sits down very close. "You breathe like a much stronger fighter than you look," the elder says quietly. "Spies breathe like that."

choices.text: Play the fool, and hold the seal

ok.log: You talk about the weather, badly, and spill your tea. In the end the elder sighs and goes back to the other side of the hall. The seal holds.

fail.log: You talk too well for a fool. The elder's hand closes on your wrist, and the seal comes apart under it in front of everyone.

choices.text: Let the seal go, here and now

effects.log: You meet the elder's eyes and let the seal go. The elder does not move for a long moment, and then bows, very slightly. The whole hall saw it.

choices.text: Excuse yourself, and be gone before dawn

effects.log: You are three valleys away by sunrise. The rumour that follows you is only that you left in a hurry.

events.text: At the city gate the captain of the watch, an old master who has seen everything twice, stops you with the tip of a scabbard. "Nobody that weak walks that light," the captain says. "Who sent you, and what are you hiding?"

choices.text: Stammer like a frightened nobody

ok.log: You stammer so convincingly that the captain waves you through with a look of pity. Nobody looks twice at you after that.

fail.log: The captain taps the scabbard once against your chest, and your seal cracks like ice. The whole gate feels what you are.

choices.text: Show the captain what you are

effects.log: You let the seal go at the gate. The captain lowers the scabbard slowly, and the watch steps back to let you pass.

choices.text: Turn back and take the long road

effects.log: You turn back and take the long road round the walls. The ferry costs 5 taels, and the seal is still whole.

events.text: Your legendary weapon wakes in the middle of a drill, and a voice like a war drum says: "Your guard is a disgrace." It is the Iron Marshal, the soul of a general who died holding a mountain pass, and it has decided you will do.

choices.text: Ask the Marshal to drill you

effects.log: The Marshal drills you until your arms shake, then once more. "Adequate," it says. From it, that is a medal.

choices.text: Answer that your guard has kept you alive

effects.log: "So did mine," says the Marshal, "until it did not." But it laughs, a short hard laugh, and stays.

events.text: You cut your hand on your own weapon, and instead of pain there is warmth, and humming. A soft voice says, "Oh, I am sorry. Let me." The cut closes. The spirit in your blade is called Willow, and it has been worried about you for a while.

choices.text: Thank Willow, and promise to be careful

effects.log: Willow hums all evening, pleased. Every wound you take after that heals a little cleaner.

choices.text: Ask why a gentle spirit sleeps in a weapon

effects.log: "Someone has to stop you swinging it at the wrong people," says Willow. You think about that for a long time.

events.text: In a quiet inn your legendary weapon starts to rattle in its scabbard, and a voice cackles: "Finally! Someone worth waking for. Who are we fighting? Is it him? Is it everybody?" The spirit calls itself Stormcrow, and it has been bored for a century.

choices.text: Promise Stormcrow a worthy opponent

effects.log: "A promise!" Stormcrow crows. "I will hold you to it." It does, every single day.

choices.text: Tell it to be quiet, you are eating

effects.log: Stormcrow sulks for three days. On the fourth it tells you a joke so good you choke on your rice. You are friends.

events.text: While you read by lamplight, a dry voice from the weapon on the table says, "That commentary is wrong, you know. I wrote the original." It is Old Ink, the spirit of a swordsman-scholar, and it has opinions about everything you have ever read.

choices.text: Ask Old Ink to correct the commentary

effects.log: Old Ink corrects it, and the next, and the next, until dawn. Your mind has never been so tired, or so sharp.

choices.text: Ask Old Ink about its own last duel

effects.log: Old Ink tells you, form by form, and at the end you understand a sword art you had only copied before.

events.text: Your boots are on the roof. Your belt is in the well. Your legendary weapon is exactly where you left it, giggling. A small voice says, "You took ages to notice me!" The spirit is called Pebble, and it is very pleased with itself.

choices.text: Laugh, and fetch your boots

effects.log: Pebble is delighted that you laughed. Things still go missing, but they turn up in lucky places now.

choices.text: Tell Pebble that partners do not hide boots

effects.log: Pebble thinks about it seriously and agrees, mostly. Your boots stay where they are. Your belt does not.

events.text: At midnight your legendary weapon goes cold in your hand, and a voice like frost says, "So you are the one who carries me now. You are softer than the last. We will fix that." The spirit names itself Ashen Fang.

choices.text: Tell Ashen Fang you will not be fixed

effects.log: Ashen Fang is silent a long while. "Stubborn," it says at last. "Good. Stubborn lasts." It stays.

choices.text: Ask Ashen Fang what it can teach you

effects.log: It teaches you, coldly and very well. Some of its lessons you decide not to learn. It notices.

events.text: One night your legendary weapon hums in its rack, and for a moment a presence looks out of the steel at you: old, proud, and not impressed. "Not you," it says. "Not yet." Then the steel is only steel again.

choices.text: Swear to become worth its waking

effects.log: You swear it aloud to an empty room. Nothing answers. The weapon seems a little heavier in your hand after that.

choices.text: Shrug. It is a good weapon either way

effects.log: You shrug and go back to bed. The weapon cuts just as well. Somewhere inside it, something keeps watching.
